t.5.16.1: As he was thus gazing over the grove of flowering trees and searching for Vaidehī, the night drew on until only a little of it remained.
t.5.16.3: Then the mighty-armed Daśagrīva, of great strength, was awakened by the sounds of auspicious musical instruments, delightful to the ear and to the mind.
t.5.16.2: And at the close of night he heard the sounds of Vedic recitation of the Brahmarakṣasas, who were learned in the Vedas with their six limbs and who performed the foremost sacrifices.
t.5.16.4: Having awakened at the proper time, the mighty lord of the rākṣasas, wearing garlands and garments that had slipped loose, began thinking of Vaidehī.
t.5.16.5: Intensely driven toward her by Madana and wild with intoxication, that rākṣasa could not conceal that desire within himself.
t.5.16.6: Adorned with every ornament and bearing unsurpassed splendour, he approached that grove, thronged with trees of many kinds laden with every sort of flower and fruit.
t.5.16.7: He beheld the grove, surrounded by lotus ponds and adorned with many kinds of flowers, made colorful by ever-exultant birds, and supremely wondrous.
t.5.16.9: He entered the Aśoka grove itself, thronged with herds of many kinds of animals, covered with fallen fruits, and dense with trees.
t.5.16.8: And gazing upon that grove, encircled by many kinds of īhāmṛgas delightful to the eye, he beheld the avenues with their archways of jewels and gold.
t.5.16.11: There some of the women took up golden lamps, some held yak-tail whisks in their hands, and others carried palm-leaf fans.
t.5.16.10: As the Paulastya went along, a hundred women followed him, just as the wives of the gods and Gandharvas follow Mahendra.
t.5.16.12: Some carried water before him in golden pitchers, while others, taking up round-tipped swords, walked behind him.
t.5.16.13: Then a certain adroit and lovely woman took up, with her right hand, a jewelled cup filled to the brim with wine.
t.5.16.14: Another woman, taking up a parasol with a golden handle, resembling a royal swan and radiant as the full moon, walked behind him.
t.5.16.15: Rāvaṇa's foremost wives, their eyes heavy with sleep and intoxication, followed their heroic lord as a streak of lightning follows a cloud.
t.5.16.16: Then that monkey, the son of the Wind, heard the jingling of the girdles and the tinkling of the anklets of those most excellent women.
t.5.16.17: And the monkey Hanumān saw him, whose deeds were incomparable and whose strength and valour were beyond imagining, as he arrived at the doorway.
t.5.16.18: Him, lit up on every side by many lamps steeped in fragrant oil and carried before him.
t.5.16.19: He was filled with lust, pride and intoxication, his long eyes coppery and sidelong, like Kandarpa himself appearing in person with his bow cast aside.
t.5.16.20: He was gracefully trailing a superb, spotless garment that resembled the foam of churned nectar, which had slipped loose and caught on his armlet.
t.5.16.21: Hidden in the leafy branches and covered by the dense mass of leaves and flowers, he began to observe closely the one who had come near.
t.5.16.22: Then, as he looked about, that elephant among monkeys saw the noble women of Rāvaṇa, endowed with beauty and youth.
t.5.16.23: Surrounded by those beautiful women, the king of great renown entered that pleasure grove, resounding with the cries of beasts and birds.
t.5.16.24: Intoxicated, decked with splendid ornaments, with ears pointed like stakes and possessed of great strength, that son of Viśravas, the lord of the Rākṣasas, was seen by him.
t.5.16.26: Thinking, "This is the mighty-armed Rāvaṇa," the monkey Hanūmān, the greatly radiant son of the Wind-god, leapt down.
t.5.16.25: Surrounded by the most excellent women, like the moon by the stars, was the one whom the great monkey of great energy beheld, that splendid, radiant one.
t.5.16.27: Even so, though himself of fierce splendour, Hanumān was overpowered by Rāvaṇa's splendour, and clinging within the hidden recesses of the leaves, he stayed concealed.
t.5.16.28: Rāvaṇa, eager to see her, approached that lady with black-tipped tresses, shapely hips, close-set breasts and dark-cornered eyes.
